title: Experimental model intake PRD with gradual pin paths and runtime gating
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD to clarify requirements for admitting experimental open-source weights into the Redwood model catalog. Defines a staged admission path (ephemeral -> probationary -> pinned), runtime gating tests, acceptable compatibility notes, and precise acceptance criteria for each phase. Purpose: reduce operational surprises from unvetted community variants while enabling discovery and fast iteration for model teams.
background: We continue to see requests from research and community contributors to add experimental weights to the catalog. Current intake has produced several incidents where model variants behaved unexpectedly under production traffic (KV cache mismatches, OOM on specific seq lengths, tokenizer differences). We need a lightweight, repeatable intake flow with clear tests, pin semantics, and rollback triggers that platform and runtime teams can operationalize.
scope: Define admission gates and observable signals for three staged states (ephemeral, probationary, pinned). Create an automated runtime sanity checklist run by the ingestion job. Specify metadata fields contributors must supply (tokenizer hash, supported sequence lengths, quantization artifacts). Document fallback policies and minimum telemetry that must be emitted.
out_of_scope: Automated full-model benchmarking against every Redwood workload, legal IP vetting (handled by Legal), and long-term model quality evaluation—those are separate initiatives.
requirements: 1) Intake manifest: every submission must include model_id, source_url, training_provenance, tokenizer_checksum, recommended_max_seq, example_inference_snippet, and optional quantization_guidance.
2) Staged states: ephemeral (unlisted, 7-day TTL), probationary (listed, limited traffic cap, 30-day evaluation), pinned (stable, eligible for routing).

3) Runtime gating: automated check suite must run on target infra (GPU/CPU) validating: model loads, KV cache correctness for prefix queries, memory usage profile for sequences at 25%, 50%, 100% of recommended_max_seq, deterministic tokenization for example inputs, and a small prompt-safety scan for adversarial tokenization behavior.

4) Compatibility note schema: free-text rationale + structured flags: tokenizer-incompatible, kv-cache-unsafe, requires-custom-kernel, incompatible-with-quantized-paths. Each flag must include a documented mitigation or fallback.

5) Pin path: explicit criteria for moving from ephemeral->probationary (all runtime gates pass + security review) and probationary->pinned (error-rate < 0.5% on probed traffic + no regression alerts for 14 days + signed-off by runtime owner).
6) Telemetry: ingestion must enable per-model token-level latency histograms, OOM/error counts, and a lightweight quality sentinel (example prompt family responses stored for regression checks).
7) Rollback and emergency delisting: define immediate delist triggers (excessive OOMs, correctness catastrophes, security exploit reports) and required post-mortem SLA (72h draft).
acceptance_criteria: A) A runnable intake job exists that accepts a manifest and produces a pass/fail with structured compatibility flags for a submitted model.

B) The runtime gating checklist is automated and produces reproducible logs that runtime engineers can inspect. Checklist covers model load, KV cache behavior on prefix tests, memory profiling, and tokenization determinism.
C) The catalog UI shows the three states with clear TTL/traffic caps and documents compatibility flags on the model page.
D) Documentation: CONTRIBUTING.md updated with required manifest fields and example submissions, plus an operator runbook for emergency delist procedures.
E) Security review required and completed for probationary promotions; the intake pipeline surfaces the security review status.
F) Metrics wired: per-model latency histogram and OOM/error counter emit to the console dashboard with one-week retention for probationary models.
G) A canary submission (team-provided toy model) has been processed end-to-end and progressed from ephemeral->probationary->pinned in a demo run following the defined criteria.
success_metrics: Metric 1: % of new open-model ingests that complete automated runtime gates within 24 hours (target >= 90%).
Metric 2: Number of production incidents attributable to unvetted ingests in a quarter (target decrease by 80% vs prior quarter).
Metric 3: Time to first usable catalog listing for community weights (goal < 48 hours for ephemeral visibility).
rollout_plan: Phase 1: implement manifest schema and gating tests (engineering spike). Phase 2: integrate intake job with catalog and console UI (limited to internal teams). Phase 3: open to community with rate limits and a lightweight contributor guide. Use one internal canary org for the first 30 days. Monitor metrics and iterate.
test_plan: Create an automated CI pipeline that runs gating tests against a matrix of representative infra instances (A100/RTX, CPU only). Include negative tests (intentionally broken tokenizer, oversized seqs) to verify gates fail safely. Add a manual QA checklist for console UI display and operator runbook verification.
tradeoffs: Tighter gating reduces incident risk but slows discovery and community adoption. We choose a lightweight first-pass (ephemeral with TTL) to balance speed and safety. Some complex kernel incompatibilities will be flagged as 'requires-custom-kernel' and may block pinning until runtime support is scheduled.
dependencies: ENG-50212 (console: model-state UI and TTL enforcement)
decision_log: 2026-02-13: Decided ephemeral TTL = 7 days to allow fast testing and automatic cleanup (decision by PM + Runtime).
2026-02-15: Agreed to require security review before moving to probationary state (SEC + PM).
2026-02-18: Opted to expose structured compatibility flags instead of permissive free-text only to aid automatic routing and fallback logic.
notes: Operator ask: provide a fast 'delist' button in the console tied to a post-action incident ticket template.
Consider adding a lightweight simulation of prefix-KV behavior in the ingest job to catch cache-only regressions early.
Follow-up: evaluate whether quantization metadata can be auto-derived for common frameworks (Torch/ONNX) in a later iteration.
